q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of imitation or fashion jewellery?
title: Imitation jewellery footprint per kg
short: Weigh the base metal, usually brass, copper or zinc alloy, and multiply by supplier figures. Add casting, polishing, electroplating, stone setting and packing energy, then divide the unit's electricity and fuel by kg passed. Plating energy can be a large share.
audience: Imitation jewellery makers, including Mumbai, Rajkot and Machilipatnam units

ul: Brass, copper or zinc alloy by weight.
Plating metals such as gold, silver, rhodium or nickel.
Electroplating baths and rectifiers, and lacquering.

p: Report per kg for a range, and per piece for a buyer's design with its weight.

example.title: Worked example: jewellery unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 7,994 / 2,000 = 3.997 kg CO2 per kg
Add base metal, plating metal and stones for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
